title: Reliable, scalable animal-to-human organ transplantation

concept.text: Concept synthesis: This innovation would make organs from animals a reliable, reproducibly supplied option for human transplantation. Success would require an animal organ to perform its essential functions in a human recipient for years, with acceptable risks and a manageable treatment burden. The intended capability combines durable organ function with dependable production and clinical delivery; a single successful operation would demonstrate only part of it.

Scope synthesis: The central biomedical engineering challenge is compatibility between a living animal organ and the human body. Organ design or modification, immune management, physiological performance, and biological safety must work together. Gene editing is part of the pig-kidney approach described in the supplied research, but neither gene editing alone nor temporary graft function would establish reliable, scalable transplantation.

significance.text: Conditional impact synthesis: A safe, durable supply of animal organs could substantially expand transplantation through a biological source that can be bred and supplied reproducibly. The direct consequence would be an additional route to organ replacement. Shorter waits, broader eligibility, or earlier transplantation would be downstream possibilities if organ availability, patient outcomes, and clinical capacity supported them; these are potential consequences rather than demonstrated outcomes.

Impact limits synthesis: Reproducible production would not make organs unlimited or automatically accessible. Availability would still depend on breeding, screening, organ quality, surgery, immune management, pathogen surveillance, cost, and transplant infrastructure. Clinical value would also depend on how the risks and treatment burden compare with appropriate existing care. Animal organs and manufactured human organs address the same supply problem through different biological sources and production processes, so progress in one does not establish feasibility or readiness in the other.

missing_breakthrough.text: Research-goal synthesis: The missing capability is sustained compatibility across several interacting systems. The proposed organ must avoid acute and chronic rejection, harmful coagulation and inflammatory responses, and progressive tissue injury while reliably performing its physiological functions. Preventing an early destructive response would be insufficient if later injury gradually undermined the graft. The supplied material identifies these as barriers but does not provide inspectable scientific evidence establishing their relative importance or showing which interventions resolve them.

Engineering synthesis: Biological safety and supply reliability must be demonstrated alongside recipient compatibility. Concrete requirements include controlling the risk of animal-pathogen transmission, maintaining reproducible donor-animal and organ quality, and making screening and surveillance workable at clinical scale. Protection achieved through intensive treatment would also need evaluation for its infection risks and practical burden. These are proposed requirements derived from the concept, not capabilities established by the available source record.

current_state.text: The supplied research attributes a report titled “Porcine kidney xenotransplantation as a bridge to allotransplantation: a first-in-human study” to Leonardo V. Riella and colleagues, dated 3 September 2026, with DOI 10.1016/S0140-6736(26)01295-X. It describes a gene-edited pig kidney supporting one living recipient without dialysis for 271 days, followed by graft failure and removal and a subsequent human kidney transplant. It also attributes rejection and later microvascular injury to that course. These remain reported claims from the supplied research: the evidence review could not verify the article identity, clinical timeline, or pathology findings from the retained material.

The access limitation is substantive. According to the supplied review, the retained PubMed artifact contains only a cookie challenge, with no title, authors, abstract, or scientific results. The research's statements that an abstract was inspected and that the journal full text returned a 403 error are not corroborated by that artifact. Consequently, this record cannot establish whether the claimed report is a published clinical study, determine its publication status, or independently confirm its results. Missing accessible evidence does not establish that the report or its findings are false.

Interpretive synthesis: If verified, 271 days without dialysis in one recipient would demonstrate a meaningful period of kidney support and potential use as a bridge to human-organ transplantation. Graft failure and removal would limit that result's implications for durable replacement, while the single-recipient scope would leave reproducibility, recipient selection, longer-term outcomes, and scalable supply unresolved. No bounded search record was supplied to establish coverage through 1 November 2026; the artifact's retrieval on 11 November 2026 does not establish how complete the account of the field is.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed clinical demonstration: Multicenter trials should show durable, organ-specific function and acceptable recipient survival, infection risk, and treatment burden relative to appropriate existing care. Protocols should specify follow-up periods, acceptance thresholds, recipient populations, and clinically meaningful outcomes in advance. For a capability intended to function for years, early postoperative success or temporary freedom from replacement therapy would be insufficient on its own. These are proposed evaluation principles, not established consensus standards.
completion_criteria.label: Multicenter trials demonstrate durable organ function and acceptable clinical outcomes

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and supply demonstration: Results should be repeatable across recipients, clinical teams, and independently produced donor organs. Evaluation should connect recipient outcomes to reproducible production, organ-quality assessment, pathogen screening, and ongoing surveillance. A convincing demonstration should also establish whether the surgery, immune-management regimen, monitoring, and supply process can be delivered with a practical treatment burden at the intended scale.
completion_criteria.label: Repeatable recipient outcomes with practical organ supply at intended scale

completion_criteria.text: Proposed boundaries of a completion claim: Evidence should state which animal source, organ type, recipient groups, treatment regimens, and duration of follow-up it covers. Successful kidney transplantation would not establish success for other organs, and a bridge-to-transplant application should be assessed separately from long-term replacement. Finite trials can establish demonstrated breadth and estimate observed risks; they cannot establish compatibility with every recipient or rule out every rare or delayed infection and graft failure.
completion_criteria.label: Completion claims state demonstrated transplantation scope and remaining risk limits

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: BME-01, “Manufacturing transplantable human organs on demand,” shares the goal of expanding organ supply, but proposes manufactured human organs rather than organs obtained from animals. BME-06, “Long-term banking of transplantable human organs,” addresses storage and availability of human organs. BME-11, “Controlled regeneration of complex organs in the adult body,” instead seeks restoration within the patient. BME-13, “Durable autonomous artificial-organ replacement,” pursues replacement through artificial systems. These are distinct routes to organ availability or restored function; success in animal-to-human transplantation would not complete any of them.

Roster-based synthesis: BME-08, “Reliable, antigen-specific immune tolerance,” overlaps directly with the immune-compatibility problem and could, conditionally, help reduce rejection or treatment burden. It would not by itself establish adequate organ physiology, control of coagulation and inflammation, pathogen safety, or reproducible supply. Conversely, a successful animal-organ transplant maintained with ongoing immune suppression would not necessarily demonstrate antigen-specific tolerance.

Roster-based synthesis: BME-02, “Programmable delivery of genetic therapies to most tissues,” concerns delivery of therapies within the body; it is distinct from modifying a donor animal or its organ. BME-10, “Validated patient-specific models for testing treatments before use,” and BME-18, “Long-lived continuous sensing of multiple clinically useful biomarkers,” could conditionally support treatment evaluation or monitoring, but neither would demonstrate transplant durability. These comparisons use the supplied roster titles; detailed specifications or evidence for the related entries were not provided.

change_log.change: Preserved BME-12 and its title while expanding the concept into a combined compatibility, durable-function, biological-safety, and supply capability.
change_log.reason: The innovation remains coherent despite the evidence gap, and both the research and review identify requirements beyond a single successful transplant.

change_log.change: Retained the reported 271-day result, clinical sequence, and injury findings with explicit attribution and uncertainty.
change_log.reason: The review found no inspectable scientific content verifying those details; that limitation warrants qualification rather than deletion or a finding that the claims are false.

change_log.change: Replaced the asserted successful abstract inspection and journal-access history with the review's documented limitation.
change_log.reason: The retained artifact contains a cookie challenge and does not corroborate either abstract inspection or a journal 403 response.

change_log.change: Separated conditional clinical significance from demonstrated outcomes and distinguished temporary bridging from durable replacement.
change_log.reason: Even if verified, a single recipient's period without dialysis would not establish years of reliable function, reproducibility, or scalable access.

change_log.change: Expanded completion proposals to include organ-specific follow-up, explicit acceptance thresholds, reproducibility, practical delivery, and bounded claims.
change_log.reason: The review identified missing protocol specificity; finite demonstrations cannot establish literal universality.

change_log.change: Used the supplied roster to explain relevant conceptual relationships while limiting comparisons to title-level scope.
change_log.reason: The final inputs provide BME-01's title and other roster entries, permitting a narrower comparison than the review could make without establishing their detailed specifications.

change_log.change: Distinguished evidence retrieval from coverage of the field through the requested as-of date.
change_log.reason: A retrieval timestamp does not substitute for a bounded search record or establish that the current-state account is comprehensive.

unresolved_issues: The identity, authorship, publication date, DOI, and publication status of the purported 2026 report require corroboration from scientific content.
The reported 271 days without dialysis, graft failure and removal, subsequent human kidney transplantation, and rejection and microvascular injury remain unverified.
The supplied material does not resolve whether an abstract was successfully inspected elsewhere or whether journal access returned a 403 error.
No bounded search record establishes coverage through 1 November 2026, so additional achievements or contrary findings may be absent.
Organ-specific follow-up periods, acceptable outcome thresholds, comparator care, recipient populations, and practical supply requirements remain to be defined.

Detailed comparisons with related concepts remain limited to the supplied roster titles. The review's recommendation to leave the BME-01 comparison wholly unassessed was narrowed because its title is now supplied; no detailed specification was inferred.

brief.title: Dependable animal organs for human transplants
possible: People who need a transplant could receive an animal organ that works for years, with manageable treatment and acceptable risks. Hospitals could draw on a dependable supply of organs bred for transplantation.
why: A reproducible source of animal organs could expand access to organ replacement. For people waiting for a transplant, that could mean shorter waits or treatment earlier in their illness.

sources.showed: A genetically modified pig kidney kept a living recipient free of dialysis, a treatment that filters blood. The kidney later failed and was removed. The patient subsequently received a human kidney.
sources.quote: The xenograft functioned immediately after transplantation on Jan 25, 2025, and sustained dialysis independence for 271 days.
sources.cited_for: The case demonstrates prolonged kidney support and a subsequent transition to a human transplant.
sources.not_established: A single recipient does not establish lasting organ replacement, repeatable outcomes or dependable supply.

sources.showed: In a single living recipient, a pig kidney removed waste, regulated dissolved salts and concentrated urine. Kidney function recovered after treatment for rejection, the body's immune attack on the organ.
sources.quote:
Despite this, the recipient
maintained blood pressure throughout the post-transplant period
(Fig. 2A).
sources.cited_for: A pig kidney can perform essential kidney functions in a living human.
sources.not_established: Short follow-up in a single recipient does not establish reliable function over years.

sources.showed: The team engineered donor pigs and tested their kidneys in monkeys. Kidneys with added human genes survived longer than those with only certain immune triggers removed.
sources.quote:
the kidneys with three glycan antigen
knockouts alone experienced poor graft survival, whereas those with glycan antigen
knockouts and human transgene expression demonstrated significantly longer
survival time
sources.cited_for: Genetic changes to donor pigs can improve kidney survival in monkeys.
sources.not_established: Survival in monkeys does not establish durable human outcomes or practical clinical supply.

shown: Riella and colleagues reported that a genetically modified pig kidney kept a living recipient free of dialysis for 271 days. Early rejection responded to treatment, but later injury to small blood vessels preceded organ failure and removal. No pig pathogen transmission was detected.

Anand and colleagues reported that engineered pig kidneys supported monkeys for up to 758 days. Lee and colleagues separately showed essential kidney functions in a living human. These results demonstrate biological compatibility over limited periods.
missing: Trials have yet to demonstrate years of reliable human organ function with acceptable survival, infection risk and treatment burden.
Outcomes must repeat across recipients, clinical teams and independently produced organs.
Dependable organ production, quality screening and infection monitoring must work together at practical clinical scale.

milestones.label: Durable function and acceptable outcomes across transplant centres
milestones.explanation: Trials across centres would have to show lasting organ function and acceptable survival, infection risk and treatment burden against existing care. This would establish clinical value beyond temporary support.

milestones.label: Repeatable outcomes with practical organ supply
milestones.explanation: Results would have to repeat across recipients, teams and independently produced organs, with workable screening, monitoring and treatment. This would connect successful surgery to dependable delivery at scale.

milestones.label: Clear boundaries for demonstrated success and remaining risks
milestones.explanation: Claims of success would have to specify animal source, organ, recipients, treatment and follow-up. This would distinguish temporary support from lasting replacement and keep conclusions within what trials demonstrate.

uncertain: The causes of late organ injury, and which treatments can prevent it without excessive infection risk, remain unresolved.
Suitable follow-up periods, acceptable outcomes and practical supply requirements still need definition for each organ and recipient group.
Finite trials cannot rule out every rare or delayed infection or organ failure.

page.title: Pig-to-human organ xenotransplantation
page.definition: Pig organs replace or support failing human organs as licensed transplant products, supported by clinical evidence for the authorised indication and validated production. Xenotransplantation means transplantation between species.

goal.need: HRSA estimates that 12 people die each day in the United States while waiting for an organ transplant. The International Xenotransplantation Association identifies the shortage of human donor organs as the reason to develop transplantation from another species.

figures.caption: U.S. transplant waiting list and transplant activity
rows: People on the national waiting list
figures.note: The waiting list is a snapshot; transplant activity is an annual flow. Subtracting them does not measure annual unmet demand.

statements.quote: IXA Council recommends that xenotransplantation should be prioritized as a global health endeavor
technologies that expand the availability of transplantable organs
statements.context: Part of the company's stated public-benefit purpose, reiterated in its quarterly filing.

completion.title: FDA licenses a pig-organ product for transplantation into living humans.
completion.criterion: For an organ case, FDA approves a Biologics License Application for a specified pig-organ product and human transplant indication under section 351(a) of the Public Health Service Act. The product satisfies safety, purity and potency requirements, and its manufacturing establishments satisfy applicable manufacturing and inspection requirements. Achievement applies to the licensed product, organ, recipient population and indication.
completion.set_by: U.S. FDA, 21 CFR 601.2(a), 601.2(d) and 601.20; the xenotransplantation-product pathway is described in FDA's December 2016 guidance.
completion.threshold_quote: the establishment(s) and the product meet applicable requirements to ensure the continued safety, purity, and potency of such products.
completion.basis: United Therapeutics identifies a Biologics License Application as the intended regulatory endpoint for its kidney and heart programmes. FDA licensure evaluates the product and its manufacturing establishments together. This supplies an external completion test encompassing clinical evidence and controlled production.

milestones.title: A transplanted pig organ demonstrates its intended biological activity in an animal model.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate the intended biological activity of a transplanted pig organ in an appropriate animal model, establishing the feasibility and rationale for the proposed human application.
milestones.set_by: U.S. FDA, November 2013 preclinical guidance, section III.B.4: proof-of-concept studies. This is a qualitative preclinical criterion, without an organ-independent survival cutoff.
milestones.threshold_quote: establish the feasibility and rationale for use of an investigational CGT product in the targeted patient population.

milestones.title: A pig organ performs its intended physiological function in a living human.
milestones.criterion: A transplanted pig organ performs its intended physiological function in a living human recipient, demonstrated by organ-specific physiological measurements.
milestones.set_by: The field's first-in-human functional-demonstration convention, recognised in the IXA's 2026 consultation, section 3.1, and applied in primary clinical case reports.
milestones.threshold_quote: demonstrate the biological feasibility and functional capability across organ systems

milestones.title: A prospective pig-organ clinical trial transplants its first living participant.
milestones.criterion: A prospective safety-and-efficacy trial actually transplants a living participant after its Investigational New Drug application takes effect, with the applicable informed-consent and institutional-review requirements satisfied. An IND normally takes effect 30 days after FDA receipt without a clinical hold, or upon earlier FDA notification.
milestones.set_by: U.S. FDA, 21 CFR 312.40, governing initiation of clinical investigations; implemented for pig kidneys in the EXPAND study.
milestones.threshold_quote: An investigator may not administer an investigational new drug to human subjects until the IND goes into effect under paragraph (b) of this section.

milestones.title: Clinical investigations establish a pig-organ product's effectiveness for its intended use.
milestones.criterion: Adequate and well-controlled clinical investigation(s) establish effectiveness for the intended indication, with confirmatory evidence when relying on one investigation. Sufficient safety data support assessment of whether benefits outweigh risks.
milestones.set_by: U.S. FDA, biologics-licensure evidence requirements in 21 CFR 601.2(a), explained in its June 2026 revised draft effectiveness guidance. The guidance is draft and not for implementation.
milestones.threshold_quote: The finding of substantial evidence of effectiveness is necessary but not sufficient for FDA approval.

milestones.title: All critical pig-organ manufacturing processes pass prospective validation at full scale.
milestones.criterion: Validate all critical processes used to manufacture the pig-organ product before licensure. FDA expects prospective validation at full scale, except for studies demonstrating viral clearance. This establishes process performance for the proposed production system. Manufacturing validation can proceed alongside clinical development; FDA's separate establishment-inspection requirements apply at licensure.
milestones.set_by: U.S. FDA, December 2016 xenotransplantation guidance, section VIII.C.5, Process Validation. These are published nonbinding recommendations preceding licensure.
milestones.threshold_quote: Ultimately, before licensure or product approval, you should validate all critical processes used to manufacture the product.

milestones.title: A transplanted pig organ performs its intended physiological function in a brain-dead human recipient.
milestones.criterion: A transplanted pig organ performs its intended physiological function in a brain-dead human recipient maintained on somatic support, demonstrated by organ-specific physiological measurements.
milestones.set_by: The field's qualitative functional-demonstration convention for decedent-model studies, recognised by the International Xenotransplantation Association's 2026 global consultation, section 3.1.
milestones.threshold_quote: decedent model investigations collectively demonstrate the biological feasibility and functional capability across organ systems and the utility of decedent models of clinical xenotransplantation.

measures.measure: Dialysis independence after pig-kidney transplantation in a living human
measures.value: 271 days in one recipient transplanted on 25 January 2025. Graft failure required removal; a human kidney transplant followed 82 days after removal.

measures.measure: Graft dysfunction and recipient survival after pig-heart transplantation
measures.value: One recipient transplanted on 7 January 2022 developed sudden xenograft dysfunction on postoperative day 49; life support was withdrawn on day 60.

measures.measure: Auxiliary pig-liver retention in a living human
measures.value: 38 days in one recipient. The auxiliary graft was removed because of xenotransplantation-associated thrombotic microangiopathy, involving small-vessel injury and clotting. The recipient died on postoperative day 171.

measures.measure: Pig-lung function in a human decedent model
measures.value: 216 hours of monitored viability and function in one brain-dead recipient. Severe oedema appeared at 24 hours, with antibody-mediated injury on postoperative days 3 and 6.

not_found: No organ-independent minimum graft-survival duration or annual production rate was found in the FDA and IXA guidance examined.
No publicly specified cohort-level efficacy success cutoff was found for EXPAND or EXPRESS.
No public report establishing full-scale validation of all critical pig-organ manufacturing processes was located.
The ClinicalTrials.gov page for NCT06878560 did not expose its study text; the sponsor's published study description supplies the EXPAND endpoints.
The Lancet and Journal of Hepatology full texts were inaccessible; their PubMed abstracts were accessible.
No FDA marketing licence for a transplanted pig solid organ was located.

results.finding: One living pig-kidney recipient had creatinine clearance of 64 mL/min/1.73 m² after rejection treatment.
results.detail: The recipient had no residual kidney function before transplantation. Acute rejection caused a temporary decline in graft function.
results.quote:
Following treatment, kidney
function recovered, reaching a CrCl of 64 mL/min/1.73 m² by POD 35
(Fig. 1A).

results.finding: One living recipient remained dialysis-independent for 271 days after pig kidney transplantation.
results.detail: The report states that the graft functioned, but the supplied text gives no organ-specific physiological measurements. The graft later failed and was removed.
results.quote: The xenograft functioned immediately after transplantation on Jan 25, 2025, and sustained dialysis independence for 271 days.

results.finding: The first recipient in a planned three-patient pig kidney study received a transplant.
results.detail: The study was conducted under an Expanded Access IND. The text does not establish a prospective safety-and-efficacy trial, when the IND took effect, or the applicable consent and institutional-review requirements.
results.quote: This report describes the first recipient in a planned three-patient study conducted under a US Food and Drug Administration Expanded Access Investigational New Drug application.

results.finding: One pig kidney recipient achieved 271 days of dialysis independence before graft failure.
results.detail: This single case provides preliminary clinical evidence of renal support, but does not establish effectiveness through adequate and well-controlled investigations or provide sufficient safety data for the required benefit-risk assessment.
results.quote: The xenograft functioned immediately after transplantation on Jan 25, 2025, and sustained dialysis independence for 271 days.

results.finding: One living recipient's pig kidney achieved creatinine clearance of 43 mL/min/1.73 m² by postoperative day 3.
results.detail: The recipient had no residual kidney function before transplantation. Acute rejection reduced clearance, which recovered after treatment.
results.quote:
The xenograft demonstrated early graft function, with a creatinine
clearance (CrCl) of 43 mL/min/1.73 m² by post-operative day (POD) 3.

results.finding: One living recipient's pig kidney sustained renal functions over 51 days of follow-up.
results.detail: This single compassionate-use case provides clinical evidence of kidney function, but it is not an adequate and well-controlled investigation establishing effectiveness or a sufficient basis for assessing the product's benefit-risk balance.
results.quote:
Over a 51 day follow-up, the xeno-
graft sustained key renal functions, including waste clearance, elec-
trolyte, volume, and blood pressure regulation.

results.finding: Engineered pig kidneys transplanted into 15 cynomolgus monkeys supported life for up to 758 days.
results.detail: Recipients received immunosuppression. The transplanted kidney filtered creatinine sufficiently to compensate for removal of the native kidneys; graft survival varied.
results.quote: renal grafts derived from the 3KO.7TG ± RI porcine donor supported life long-term in cynomolgus monkeys, up to 758 days.

results.finding: In 5 low-risk baboon recipients, transplanted pig kidneys maintained stable graft function for 165–337 days.
results.detail: Both native kidneys were removed. One additional recipient experienced hyperacute rejection.
results.quote: All recipients with low levels of preformed anti-source pig Nabs accepted their grafts and maintained stable graft function for 337, 285, 278, 252, and 165 days (Figs.

results.finding: Gene-edited pig hearts supported 8 of 15 baboons for more than one month.
results.detail: The pediatric-sized baboon model assessed pig hearts as a bridge to allotransplantation. Donor genetics and treatment protocols varied across experiments.
results.quote: Eight of 15 baboons survived >1 month with a functioning xenograft.

results.finding: Three of five EGEN-2784 kidney recipients had kidney function without dialysis for more than eight months.
results.detail: The recipients had kidney failure and received the transplants under expanded access.
results.quote: Three of these patients have achieved sustained kidney function for more than eight months without the need for dialysis.

results.finding: FDA cleared a Phase 1/2/3 EGEN-2784 trial planned for 33 patients.
results.detail: The trial was expected to begin in the first quarter of 2027; the release does not report a trial participant receiving a transplant.
results.quote: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has cleared eGenesis to conduct a Phase 1/2/3 trial (RESTORE) to evaluate EGEN-2784 in 33 patients with kidney failure who are between 50 and 70 years of age and waitlisted for a human donor kidney transplant.

results.finding: Three of five expanded-access recipients had kidney function without dialysis for more than eight months.
results.detail: These preliminary outcomes do not establish effectiveness through adequate and well-controlled clinical investigation or provide sufficient safety data for a benefit-risk assessment.
results.quote: Three of these patients have achieved sustained kidney function for more than eight months without the need for dialysis.

results.finding: One living recipient of a genetically modified pig heart had cardiac output of 5.0 to 6.0 liters per minute.
results.detail: ECMO was discontinued on day 4. The graft subsequently failed on day 49, and life support was withdrawn on day 60.
results.quote: The cardiac output ranged from 5.0 to 6.0 liters per minute, and the stroke volume ranged from 65 to 70 ml per square meter of body-surface area.

results.finding: In 1 living recipient, an auxiliary pig liver secreted bile and corrected coagulation before removal on day 38.
results.detail: The graft was removed because of xenotransplantation-associated thrombotic microangiopathy; the patient died on day 171.
results.quote: The porcine graft exhibited metabolically active liver function, bile secretion, and coagulation correction, demonstrating not only survival but clinically meaningful function.

results.finding: EXPAND reported its first UKidney transplant in 1 living participant.
results.detail: The release describes a prospective safety-and-efficacy study but does not state when its IND took effect or whether informed-consent and institutional-review requirements were satisfied.

results.finding: Pig liver xenografts supported life for nearly one month in 2 of 4 baboon recipients.
results.detail: Recipients received continuous human coagulation factor infusion and immunosuppression. One long-surviving recipient had de novo coagulation factor and fibrinogen production; both long-surviving animals were euthanized following complications.
results.quote: Thus, nearly one-month rejection-free survival has been achieved following LXT in 2 of 4 continuous recipients, demonstrating that the porcine liver can support life in primates for several weeks and is encouraging for potential clinical application of LXT as a bridge to allotransplantation

results.finding: Pig lung xenografts in baboons: 3 of 4 exhibited initial life-supporting function.
results.detail: Function was tested by temporarily obstructing blood flow to the native lung. Tracheal flooding occurred within 8 hours in all but one experiment in this group.

GalTKO.hCD46

results.finding: In one brain-dead human recipient, a transplanted pig kidney produced urine with concentration >600 mOsm/kg.
results.detail: The nephrectomized recipient was maintained on somatic support. Urine concentration was measured during ongoing vasopressin infusion; dialysis independence was also achieved.
results.quote: After an initial period of polyuria, UOP normalized within the first three days with urine concentration >600 mOsm/kg displayed within the first week post-transplant in the setting of ongoing exogenous vasopressin infusion.

results.finding: Pig heart transplants in 2 brain-dead recipients functioned throughout a 66-hour study.
results.detail: The abstract reports monitored hemodynamics and cardiac function, but the supplied text does not give hemodynamic measurement results demonstrating pumping function or explicitly describe somatic support. Cardiac function declined in one recipient, attributed to donor–recipient size mismatch.
results.quote: Although both xenografts demonstrated excellent cardiac function immediately after transplantation and continued to function for the duration of the study, cardiac function declined postoperatively in one case, attributed to a size mismatch between the donor pig and the recipient.

results.finding: In one brain-dead recipient, a transplanted pig liver produced 66.5 ml of bile by postoperative day 10.
results.detail: The liver was transplanted as an auxiliary graft. Porcine albumin also increased, though the authors considered bile and albumin production unlikely to support a human body long-term.
results.quote: Two hours after portal vein reperfusion of the xenograft, goldish bile was produced, increasing to 66.5 ml by postoperative day 10.

results.finding: In 1 brain-deceased recipient, a transplanted pig liver produced albumin and bile throughout 11 days.
results.detail: Production was relatively low, with late hepatic functional decline, microthrombosis and coagulation abnormalities.
results.quote: Here we report the orthotopic pig-to-human liver xenotransplantation in a brain-deceased individual. Throughout the 11-day observation period, the xenograft maintains continuous albumin and bile production with normal composition, albeit at a relatively low level.

results.finding: In one brain-dead recipient, a transplanted pig lung was reported functional over 216 hours of monitoring.
results.detail: The supplied text does not report organ-specific physiological measurements or explicitly describe somatic support. Severe edema developed at 24 hours, and antibody-mediated rejection appeared to contribute to graft damage.
results.quote: The lung xenograft maintained viability and functionality over the course of the 216 hours of the monitoring period, without signs of hyperacute rejection or infection.
